report.tagline: A scheduling link that lets people book time on your calendar without back-and-forth emails.
report.simpleSummary: Calendly ends the 'When are you free?' email chain. You connect your calendar and share a link. The other person opens it, sees your free slots and picks one, and the meeting appears in both calendars with a video link. Every person who books through your link sees Calendly, and many sign up themselves, which is how it grew to more than 50 million users with little advertising.

overview.whatItDoes: Calendly connects to your Google, Outlook or iCloud calendar and creates a booking page with your available times. People pick a slot, and Calendly sends invites, reminders and video links. Teams use it to route leads to the right salesperson, share bookings in round-robin and collect payments. In 2026 it added an AI Notetaker and Callie, an email assistant that schedules for you.
howItWorks: You sign up free and connect your calendar.
You create event types, such as a 30-minute intro call, with rules for buffers and notice.
You share your link by email, on your website or in your signature.
The invitee picks a time in their own time zone; both calendars update and a Zoom or Meet link is added.
Reminders reduce no-shows, and follow-up emails go out after the meeting.
Paid plans add more event types, team routing, payments, integrations and AI features.
overview.valueProposition: Book meetings in one step instead of five emails, with fewer no-shows and the right person on the call.

businessModel.summary: Calendly makes money from per-seat subscriptions. Individuals can use it free with one event type; professionals and teams pay monthly for more features, routing, integrations and AI.

revenueStreams.detail: $10 to $18 per seat per month billed yearly, for individuals.
$16 to $24 per seat per month billed yearly, with routing and CRM links.
From about $15,000 a year with a 50-seat minimum, security and support.

businessModel.pricing: Free: one event type and one calendar. Standard $10, Standard Plus $18, Teams $16, Teams Plus $24 per seat per month billed yearly (higher monthly). Enterprise from $15,000 a year. September 2026.
costDrivers: AI computing for Notetaker and Callie
businessModel.unitEconomics: A sales team of 10 on Teams pays 10 x $16 x 12 = $1,920 a year. Serving them costs very little because a booking page is light to host, so gross margin is likely above 85%. Winning individual users is almost free because invitees sign up after seeing the product. AI Notetaker adds real per-meeting cost, which is why it sits only on Plus plans. Rough estimates.

howTheyGetUsers: Viral loop: every booking shows Calendly to someone new
'Powered by Calendly' branding on free pages

growth.moat: Calendly's brand is so strong that 'send me your Calendly' is common. But the core feature is easy to copy, and Google Calendar, Microsoft Outlook, HubSpot and Zoom all offer booking pages. Its moat is team features like routing and integrations that sales teams depend on.

pmLessons: The best growth loops are built into the product: every Calendly booking shows the product to a new person.
A simple feature can build a big brand, but bundled rivals can copy it, so you need deeper team features.
Free plan limits must be set carefully: too tight and users leave for rivals, too loose and nobody pays.
Think about the other side of the experience: the invitee, who never chose your product.

interviewQuestions.question: Explain Calendly's viral loop and how you would measure it.
interviewQuestions.hint: Host shares link, invitee books, invitee sees branding, invitee signs up. Measure invitee-to-host conversion and viral coefficient.

interviewQuestions.question: Google Calendar now offers free booking pages. How should Calendly respond?
interviewQuestions.hint: Go deeper on teams (routing, CRM), cross-calendar, AI. Don't fight on basic features.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you improve the invitee experience?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find invitee pain (feels pushed work, time zones), ideas like suggested times, track booking rate.

interviewQuestions.question: What is Calendly's north star metric?
interviewQuestions.hint: Meetings booked. Break into active hosts, bookings per host, invitee conversion, paid seats.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Calendly make the free plan more generous?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh viral growth against conversion. Suggest a test and measure total revenue over a year.
